sentence_stem: If only I had studied harder,
correct_completion: I would have passed the exam.
full_sentence: If only I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
acceptable_variants: I would have got a better grade.
I would have done much better.

options.text: I would pass the exam tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: 'If only' with a past perfect expresses regret about the past, so a future-tense completion does not match the stem.
This uses the present simple to describe a habit. It does not express regret about the past.

options.text: I would have passed the exam.
I passed the exam last week.
options.why_wrong: This states a real past fact. 'If only' expresses an unreal wish, so the completion needs 'would have' to show the imagined result.

grammar_focus: Third conditional with 'if only' (unreal wish about the past)
explanation: 'If only' plus past perfect expresses a wish about a past situation that did not happen. The main clause must use 'would have' plus a past participle to show the imagined result. Polish speakers may use a simple conditional here because Polish marks the conditional with a particle and does not separate the past perfect from the simple past.
translation: Gdybym tylko uczyl sie ciezej, zdalbym egzamin.
